encounters.title: The Mane Hall Audience
encounters.description: The Lion Dominion flagship is a cathedral of gold and marble drifting through the Shattered Prides. Lord Mane himself stands at the viewport, his silver-streaked mane catching the starlight. He doesn't turn when Aristotle enters. 'I know why you're here, cat. Everyone who comes to my court wants something. The question is whether you have anything worth trading for it.'

choices.text: Offer a tribute of whisper crystals as a show of good faith

outcome.description: Lord Mane finally turns, golden eyes appraising. 'A pirate who understands diplomacy. Perhaps there's hope for the feline species after all.' He accepts the tribute with a barely perceptible nod — the closest thing to warmth a Lion lord offers.

choices.text: Propose a strategic alliance against the growing threats

outcome.description: Lord Mane's tail swishes — the only crack in his composure. 'Alliance? With a corsair?' He paces the length of the viewport. 'The Prides are fracturing. Perhaps an outsider's perspective has value.' He doesn't say yes. He doesn't say no. In Lion politics, that's practically an embrace.

choices.text: Remind him that you control the crystal supply — and his fleet runs on it

outcome.description: The temperature in the room drops ten degrees. Lord Mane's claws extend, scoring the marble floor. 'Threats, pirate? In my own hall?' Guards materialize from the shadows. But he waves them off. 'Leave. And remember — lions have very long memories.'

encounters.title: The Iron Challenge
encounters.description: The Wolf warship drops out of warp with weapons hot, its hull scarred with a hundred battles. Iron Fang's voice crackles over comms — a low, rumbling growl that vibrates the bridge. 'Cat captain. I've heard you're the one hoarding the crystals. In the Expanse, we take what we need. Prove you deserve to keep them.'

choices.text: Accept the challenge — ship to ship, as the wolves demand

outcome.description: The battle is brutal and beautiful. Iron Fang fights with savage precision, but Aristotle's ship is faster, trickier. After exchanging salvos that light up the void, Iron Fang breaks off with a bark of laughter. 'Not bad, cat. Not bad at all. You fight like a wolf born in the wrong body.'

choices.text: Offer crystals instead of combat — wolves need fuel too

outcome.description: Iron Fang goes quiet for a long moment. 'You'd rather trade than fight? Hmph.' The weapons power down. 'Smart, maybe. But in the Expanse, strength is the only currency that doesn't depreciate. Remember that.' He accepts the crystals with grudging respect.

choices.text: Full power to engines — outrun the wolf pack

outcome.description: Aristotle punches the crystal drive to maximum. The ship screams through the Expanse, Wolf fighters snapping at its wake. He escapes — barely. Iron Fang's final transmission is a single word: 'Coward.' It'll follow Aristotle through every Wolf territory from now on.

encounters.title: The Luminous Garden
encounters.description: Deep in the Fairy Realms, where crystal formations grow like flowers and the void itself shimmers with bioluminescence, a tiny figure perches on an asteroid no bigger than a house. Glimmer's wings catch every colour that exists and several that shouldn't. She waves at Aristotle's ship like she's been expecting him. She probably has.

choices.text: Approach slowly and introduce yourself

outcome.description: Glimmer zips aboard through an airlock seal that definitely shouldn't have opened. 'Oh! You're the crystal cat everyone's arguing about!' She produces a crystal that pulses in perfect sync with the ship's drive. 'I grew this for you. It'll help your ship sing better.' Her laugh sounds like wind chimes in zero gravity.

choices.text: Ask about the crystal formations growing wild here

outcome.description: Glimmer's eyes go wide with delight. 'Oh, you want to LEARN? Nobody ever wants to learn!' She launches into an explanation of crystal botany that's half science, half poetry, and entirely fascinating. By the end, Aristotle understands crystal resonance in ways no textbook could teach.

choices.text: These wild crystals are worth a fortune — start harvesting

outcome.description: Glimmer's glow dims to almost nothing. 'Oh. You're one of THOSE.' She doesn't stop him, but every crystal he takes feels heavier than it should. The garden is poorer when he leaves, and Glimmer watches from her asteroid, a fading light in the rearview.

encounters.title: The Clockwork Cavern
encounters.description: The Goblin Warrens are a maze of salvaged technology and improvised engineering. At their heart, in a chamber that ticks and whirs like a mechanical heartbeat, sits Cogsworth — a goblin who traded scrap for scholarship. His workspace is a museum of disassembled starship drives, each one labelled in meticulous handwriting that seems at odds with the chaos around it.

choices.text: Commission a crystal drive upgrade from the goblin engineer

outcome.description: Cogsworth adjusts his magnifying monocle and grins — all teeth and enthusiasm. 'Oh yes, YES! I've been theorising about resonance amplification for YEARS!' He disappears into his workshop. Hours later, he emerges with an upgrade that shouldn't work but absolutely does. 'Tell no one where you got this. My reputation, you understand.'

choices.text: Share your crystal resonance data in exchange for his research

outcome.description: Cogsworth's eyes light up behind his monocle. 'DATA! Real field data!' He practically vibrates as he pores over the readings. In return, he shares blueprints that would make a League engineer weep with envy. 'A fair exchange, captain. The pursuit of knowledge transcends faction lines.'

choices.text: Distract him and copy his research files

outcome.description: Cogsworth is trusting — too trusting. While he brews tea, Aristotle downloads everything. The data is invaluable. But as the ship pulls away from the Warrens, there's a hollow feeling in Aristotle's chest that no crystal can fill.

encounters.title: The Knight's Oath
encounters.description: The Knight Kingdoms' border station is a fortress of ancient alloy and unwavering tradition. Ser Galvain meets Aristotle at the airlock in full ceremonial armour — polished to a mirror shine, sword at his hip, every inch the chivalric ideal. 'Captain Aristotle. Your reputation precedes you.' His tone suggests the reputation is... mixed.

choices.text: Bow to Knight custom and request formal audience

outcome.description: Ser Galvain's posture softens — barely. 'You know our ways. That is... unexpected from a corsair.' He escorts Aristotle through the station with growing respect. Over a meal that follows sixteen courses of etiquette, a genuine connection forms. 'Perhaps honour is not exclusive to those who wear armour.'

choices.text: Propose a crystal-for-passage trade agreement

outcome.description: Galvain considers the offer with the gravity of a judge weighing a soul. 'Commerce is not dishonourable, provided both parties deal in good faith.' He extends a gauntleted hand. 'You have passage through Knight space, captain. Do not make me regret this.'

choices.text: Tell him his traditions are relics of a dead age

outcome.description: Ser Galvain's hand moves to his sword hilt with mechanical precision. 'You insult not me, pirate, but everything the Orders stand for.' The airlock seals behind Aristotle with emphatic finality. 'Leave. And pray we do not meet on the field.'

encounters.title: The Old Salt
encounters.description: Tidewalker's vessel is a relic — a pre-war cruiser held together by stubbornness and superlative engineering. The old dog captain sits in a chair that's been bolted to the same spot for thirty years, watching the stars with eyes that have seen everything and forgotten nothing. 'Sit down, cat. I don't stand on ceremony and my knees don't stand for much else.'

choices.text: Sit down and listen to the old captain's stories

outcome.description: Tidewalker talks for hours — about the wars he's survived, the friends he's buried, the truths he's learned. 'Cats and dogs, pirates and soldiers — we're all just passing through, son. The void doesn't care about our flags.' When Aristotle leaves, he carries navigation data to routes that aren't on any chart.

choices.text: Ask for his help navigating dangerous territory

outcome.description: Tidewalker scratches behind one floppy ear. 'Help a cat pirate? My superiors would have me court-martialled.' He pauses. 'Good thing I outrank most of them.' He transmits a set of coordinates and patrol schedules that will save Aristotle's life more than once.

choices.text: Demand League patrol routes — you know he has them

outcome.description: Tidewalker's weathered face hardens. 'Demand? From me?' He stands — slowly, painfully, but with a dignity that fills the room. 'Get off my ship, cat. And learn some manners before you get yourself killed.'

encounters.title: The Shadow Queen
encounters.description: Lady Penumbra does not receive guests in the light. Her quarters aboard the Lion diplomatic vessel are draped in shadow, illuminated only by a single whisper crystal that casts everything in pale blue. She is the power behind half the Lion Dominion's court decisions, and she knows it. 'Captain Aristotle. I've been watching your career with great interest.'

choices.text: Accept her offer to work together against the Lion hardliners

outcome.description: Lady Penumbra's smile is barely visible in the darkness. 'Smart cat. The hardliners would burn the Prides to ashes rather than share power. Together, we can save what matters.' She offers a clawed hand — delicate, deadly, and utterly sincere. A dangerous ally, but the best kind.

choices.text: Discuss terms — what exactly does she need, and what's in it for you?

outcome.description: Lady Penumbra appreciates directness. 'I need crystal supply guarantees for the moderate prides. In return, I offer intelligence on every faction that has ever visited this court.' The data she provides is staggeringly comprehensive. She has been planning this for a long time.

choices.text: Decline — you don't play shadow games

outcome.description: The crystal flickers. Lady Penumbra's expression doesn't change. 'A pity. I do hope you reconsider before the hardliners make their move.' The dismissal is elegant and absolute. Aristotle leaves feeling like he just declined the last lifeboat on a sinking ship.

encounters.title: Scrapyard Showman
encounters.description: The Goblin Warrens are chaos given physical form, and Rustclaw is their unofficial mascot. The goblin stands atop a mountain of salvaged ship parts, wearing a cape made from hull plating and a crown of circuit boards. 'WELCOME, WELCOME to Rustclaw's Emporium of Everything! You break it, you bought it! You buy it, it's probably already broken!'

choices.text: Browse the Emporium — there might be something useful in this junk

outcome.description: Buried under seventeen layers of actual garbage, Aristotle finds a pre-war crystal amplifier in near-perfect condition. Rustclaw sells it for a fraction of its value, cackling the whole time. 'You got TASTE, cat! Come back anytime! Bring salvage!'

choices.text: Ask if Rustclaw knows anyone who can modify your ship

outcome.description: 'MODIFY? I AM the modification!' Rustclaw scurries aboard uninvited and starts rewiring things. The results are terrifying and surprisingly effective. The ship now makes a worrying humming noise, but it's faster. Rustclaw refuses payment. 'Art is its own reward!'

choices.text: This place is a death trap. Leave before something explodes.

outcome.description: Aristotle backs away slowly as something in the scrap pile sparks ominously. Rustclaw shouts after him: 'YOUR LOSS, CAT! I HAD A PERFECTLY GOOD PLASMA CANNON IN HERE SOMEWHERE!' An explosion punctuates the sentence. Rustclaw's laughter echoes through the debris.

encounters.title: The Song Between Stars
encounters.description: There is no ship. There is no station. There is only a voice in the void — a transmission on a frequency that predates radio technology. The Void Singer speaks in harmonics that make whisper crystals resonate in sympathy, and her words arrive in Aristotle's mind before they reach his ears. 'You carry the crystal's song in your bones, captain. I have been listening to you for a very long time.'

choices.text: Open your mind to the Void Singer's transmission

outcome.description: The universe unfolds. Aristotle sees the crystal network that connects every realm — a web of resonance that pulses like a living heartbeat. The Void Singer shows him nodes, pathways, secrets buried in the harmonic structure of reality itself. When it ends, he can hear the crystals singing. He will always hear them now.

choices.text: Ask about the origin of whisper crystals

outcome.description: The Void Singer's response comes in images, feelings, ancient memories. The crystals were not discovered — they were planted. By whom, she cannot say. But she shows Aristotle a direction: beyond the Warp Marches, where the oldest songs still echo. 'Follow the harmony, captain. The source awaits.'

choices.text: Block the signal — nothing good comes from voices in the void

outcome.description: Aristotle slams the comms to static. The crystal drive flickers in protest, and for one terrible moment, every crystal aboard dims. Then normality returns. But sometimes, in the quiet watches, he thinks he can still hear her singing. Just barely. Just enough to wonder.

encounters.title: The Ossuary
encounters.description: In the deepest reaches of the Bone Yard, where dead ships are stacked so thick they form artificial gravity, Brother Hemlock tends his garden. The old badger monk has turned a derelict carrier into a sanctuary — hydroponics bays where plants grow between shattered bulkheads, meditation chambers in emptied torpedo bays. He greets Aristotle with tea and silence.

choices.text: Accept the tea and sit in silence with the old monk

outcome.description: They sit for an hour without speaking. The tea is excellent. When Aristotle finally rises to leave, Brother Hemlock hands him a crystal wrapped in cloth. 'This one has been singing your name. I've been keeping it safe.' The crystal is ancient, perfectly formed, and warm to the touch.

choices.text: Ask about the ships that died here — and the crews who didn't leave

outcome.description: Brother Hemlock's eyes grow distant. 'Every ship here was someone's home. I tend their memory.' He leads Aristotle through corridors lined with names — thousands of them, etched into the hull by hand. 'Remember them, captain. The void forgets. We must not.'

choices.text: The derelicts here are full of salvage — start stripping them

outcome.description: Brother Hemlock doesn't try to stop him. He just watches, tea growing cold in his paws, as Aristotle's crew tears apart the ships he's tended for decades. 'Take what you need, captain. I hope it fills whatever hollow drives you.' It doesn't.

encounters.title: The Pack Hunter
encounters.description: Snarl doesn't announce herself. One moment the sensors are clear; the next, three Wolf frigates have you bracketed in a kill box. Her voice comes through on a tight beam — low, hungry, amused. 'The crystal cat. My pack has been tracking you for six systems. You're faster than I expected. But nobody outruns the pack forever.'

choices.text: Power weapons and break the kill box

outcome.description: Aristotle fights like a cornered cat — which is exactly what he is. He cripples one frigate and clips another before Snarl calls off the pursuit. 'Impressive. You've earned a head start, cat. Next time, I won't hold back.' Her laughter echoes through the comms as the pack melts into the void.

choices.text: Jettison a crystal cache as a distraction and run

outcome.description: The crystals tumble into space, sparkling like bait. Snarl's pack breaks formation to collect them — wolves can't resist easy prey. Aristotle punches through the gap and runs. 'Clever trick,' Snarl transmits. 'But tricks only work once.'

choices.text: Surrender your cargo and negotiate passage

outcome.description: Snarl boards personally. She's smaller than expected — compact, scarred, with amber eyes that miss nothing. She takes what she wants and leaves the rest. 'Smart enough to live another day, cat. I respect that more than bravery.' She leaves him enough fuel to limp to port.

encounters.title: The Old Admiral
encounters.description: Admiral Brass commands the League's Third Fleet from the bridge of a dreadnought that dwarfs everything in the sector. The ship is immaculate, the crew terrified, and the Admiral himself is a grizzled bulldog who has fought in every major engagement for forty years. 'So you're the pirate who thinks he can play kingmaker with crystal fuel. Let me explain how the real world works.'

choices.text: Stand your ground — remind him that his fleet runs on YOUR crystals

outcome.description: Admiral Brass goes very still. Then, unexpectedly, he laughs — a deep, rumbling sound. 'Got spine, I'll give you that. Most people can't even hold eye contact.' He pours two glasses of something amber. 'Alright, pirate. Let's talk like adults.'

choices.text: Offer a long-term crystal supply contract at fair rates

outcome.description: The Admiral reviews the terms with the same intensity he brings to battle plans. 'Fair terms. Reliable supply. No political strings.' He signs with a decisive scratch of his pen. 'Don't disappoint me, pirate. I protect my supply lines — and I eliminate my problems.'

choices.text: Tell the Admiral to make an appointment like everyone else and leave

outcome.description: Admiral Brass's face turns an impressive shade of red. 'Nobody walks out on me.' Warning shots bracket Aristotle's ship as he burns for open space. He makes it — barely. The Admiral's voice follows him: 'You just made the worst enemy of your life, pirate.'

encounters.title: The Hidden Eye
encounters.description: The cartographer's map leads to a place that shouldn't exist — a pocket dimension folded into the Fairy Realms like a page hidden between chapters. The Oracle waits in a chamber of living crystal, her form shifting between states of matter. She has no face, but Aristotle feels her gaze like sunlight on closed eyes. 'You found me. That means you were meant to find me. Sit. I have things to show you.'

choices.text: Open your mind to the Oracle's visions

outcome.description: The visions come in a torrent — futures branching like crystal formations, each choice spawning a thousand consequences. Aristotle sees the Cradle of Whispers, the final battle, outcomes both glorious and catastrophic. When it ends, he gasps like a drowning man surfacing. 'The path is yours to choose,' the Oracle whispers. 'But now you choose with open eyes.'

choices.text: Ask about a specific threat — who is your greatest enemy?

outcome.description: The Oracle's form solidifies for a moment — something like sadness crossing her crystalline features. 'Your greatest enemy is the one you haven't met yet. But they have already met you — in a future they are trying to prevent.' She gives him a name. A location. A date. 'Be ready.'

choices.text: Some things are better not known. Leave.

outcome.description: The Oracle doesn't protest. 'Wisdom and cowardice look identical from the outside. Only time reveals which is which.' The pocket dimension folds shut behind Aristotle, leaving him floating in the Fairy Realms with nothing but the memory of crystal light and the nagging feeling he just made a terrible mistake.

encounters.title: The Last Archive
encounters.description: Miles deep inside the Bone Yard, past layers of dead ships that span millennia, something still has power. The Keeper's domain is a vast data archive preserved in crystal memory — the collected knowledge of civilisations that rose and fell while the stars burned. The Keeper herself is ancient, hunched, wrapped in robes woven from optical fibre. Her eyes glow with the pale light of stored data. 'Another seeker. They always come eventually.'

choices.text: Ask the Keeper about the true nature of whisper crystals

outcome.description: The Keeper pulls a crystal from the archive wall. It plays memories — not hers, but the crystals' own. They remember being planted, grown, nurtured by hands that are no longer hands. 'The crystals are seeds,' the Keeper says. 'Seeds of what, you'll have to ask the Gardeners. If any still live.' She gives Aristotle a data crystal heavier than worlds.

choices.text: Offer your own data in exchange for the Keeper's archives

outcome.description: The Keeper examines Aristotle's navigational data, faction records, and crystal readings with trembling hands. 'Fresh data. Living data. You have no idea how precious this is.' In return, she opens a section of the archive that maps the pre-war crystal distribution network — a treasure map spanning the multiverse.

choices.text: This archive is too valuable to leave in one person's hands — take it

outcome.description: The Keeper doesn't resist. She just touches the archive wall, and every crystal goes dark. 'What you take by force dies in your hands. This was always the lesson.' Millennia of knowledge, gone. Aristotle is left holding dead crystals in an empty tomb.

encounters.title: Pocket Full of Trouble
encounters.description: The Twilight Bazaar is the only place where every faction rubs shoulders without immediate bloodshed. Jinx finds Aristotle at a noodle stand — a scrawny calico cat with mismatched eyes, fingerless gloves, and a grin that promises expensive problems. 'Hey, captain. I hear you need someone who's really, really good at getting into places they shouldn't be. That's me. I'm the best. Also, someone is currently trying to kill me. So maybe we could discuss employment while running?'

choices.text: Welcome aboard — start running and explain on the way

outcome.description: The next five minutes are a blur of alleys, explosions, and Jinx's non-stop commentary. By the time they reach the ship, Aristotle has a new crew member and three new enemies. Jinx collapses into a bunk and grins. 'Best interview I've ever had. When do I start?'

choices.text: Help her escape, but no promises about employment

outcome.description: Aristotle helps Jinx lose her pursuers through the Bazaar's maintenance tunnels. She's impressive — quick, clever, and completely fearless. At the ship's airlock, she pauses. 'I owe you one, captain. If you ever need a door opened or a safe cracked, you know where to find me.' She disappears into the crowd like smoke.

choices.text: Not your problem. Finish your noodles.

outcome.description: Jinx stares for a moment, then shrugs with the resignation of someone who's been refused before. 'Fair enough.' She vanishes into the crowd. The noodles taste like regret.

encounters.title: Outstanding Balance
encounters.description: He appears without warning — a tall, thin figure in an immaculate suit that looks deeply wrong against the Bazaar's chaos. The Debt Collector doesn't carry weapons. He doesn't need them. He carries a ledger, and in that ledger is every debt ever owed in the multiverse. 'Captain Aristotle. I believe we have... an accounting to settle.'

choices.text: Pay what you owe — crystals, salvage, whatever it takes

outcome.description: The Debt Collector examines each crystal with a jeweller's eye, counts the salvage to the gram, and makes a precise notation in his ledger. 'Account settled. For now.' He snaps the book shut. 'I'll be seeing you, captain. Everyone accrues new debts.' He walks away through a crowd that parts like water.

choices.text: Negotiate — offer information instead of resources

outcome.description: The Debt Collector tilts his head, considering. 'Information has value. Location of a crystal cache? Knowledge of a faction's secret? Yes, this could... adjust the balance.' He accepts Aristotle's intelligence and makes a new notation. 'Partial payment accepted. The remainder accrues interest.'

choices.text: Tell him to take a walk — you don't owe anyone anything

outcome.description: The Debt Collector doesn't argue. He simply makes a notation in the ledger and closes it with a gentle click. 'Noted. Interest compounds, captain. And I always collect.' He walks away. Over the next week, three of Aristotle's best deals fall through, his crystal drives develop faults, and every faction he contacts seems oddly reluctant to trade.

encounters.title: The Old Mentor
encounters.description: Patch's ship is barely holding together — a battered trader vessel that's more patch than hull, which is either ironic or prophetic. The one-eyed tabby cat meets Aristotle at the airlock with a weathered smile and a bottle of something potent. 'Well well. My best student, come home at last. You look older. Good. Means you're learning.'

choices.text: Ask Patch for advice about the crystal discovery

outcome.description: Patch pours two glasses and settles into his captain's chair with a creak. 'Crystals, huh? Big prize. Bigger target.' He spends an hour teaching Aristotle things that aren't in any manual — how to read faction politics, when to bluff, when to run. 'The crystal makes you valuable. Don't let it make you a target.' He slips Aristotle a data chip. 'Old smuggling routes. Still work, last I checked.'

choices.text: Offer to repair Patch's ship — he clearly needs it

outcome.description: Patch tries to refuse — stubborn old cat — but Aristotle's crew is already on the hull. When they're done, the ship hums like it hasn't in years. Patch blinks his one good eye rapidly. 'Didn't teach you that,' he mutters. 'Must've learned it somewhere better.' He clasps Aristotle's shoulder. 'Proud of you, son.'

choices.text: Good to see you, Patch, but I've outgrown the starting realm

outcome.description: Something flickers across Patch's face — pride, maybe, or loss. 'Course you have. That was always the plan.' He raises his glass. 'To the student who surpassed the teacher. Now get out there and make me rich by association.' His laugh follows Aristotle to the airlock.

encounters.title: The Shifting Merchant
encounters.description: The ship — if it is a ship — changes shape as Aristotle watches. One moment it's a sleek yacht, the next a blocky freighter, then something with too many angles to be real. Flux steps out of an airlock that wasn't there a second ago, their form settling into something approximately humanoid. Approximately. 'Greetings, Captain Aristotle. I've been trading in this sector for... longer than your species has had names. Would you like to see my wares?'

choices.text: Show me what you've got — and explain what you are while you're at it

outcome.description: Flux's 'shop' exists in a space that doesn't obey physics. Shelves extend in impossible directions, holding artifacts from civilisations that won't exist for a million years. 'What am I? A traveller. A collector. Someone who finds the gaps between things interesting.' They sell Aristotle a crystal resonance amplifier that works on principles no one has invented yet. 'Fair price,' Flux says, shifting into something with more tentacles. 'Come back when you're ready for the really interesting items.'

choices.text: Ask about a particular alien artifact detected in deep space

outcome.description: Flux's form stills — the first time they've stopped shifting. 'Ah. You found one of the markers.' Their voice drops to something almost serious. 'The artifacts are breadcrumbs. Left by the ones who planted the crystals. Follow them far enough and you'll find the Cradle.' They hand Aristotle a set of coordinates. 'Free of charge. Consider it... an investment in an interesting future.'

choices.text: Something this alien can't be trusted — weapons hot

outcome.description: Aristotle's weapons pass through Flux like light through glass. The alien sighs — a sound like dimensions folding. 'How disappointing. Your species usually takes longer to try that.' The ship-that-isn't-a-ship folds in on itself and vanishes, leaving a faint trace of exotic particles and profound embarrassment.

encounters.title: The Crystal Healer
encounters.description: Sister Meridian's clinic occupies a converted cargo bay at the edge of the Twilight Bazaar — neutral ground where she treats anyone who walks in, regardless of faction. The fairy healer's wings are the colour of dawn, and her hands glow faintly as she works. She looks up from a patient — a Wolf marine with a shattered leg — and nods. 'With you in a moment, captain. Life doesn't pause for appointments.'

choices.text: Wait until she's finished — some things are more important than your schedule

outcome.description: Aristotle waits. An hour passes. Two. Sister Meridian finishes with the Wolf, a Goblin with chemical burns, and a Lion cub with a fever before turning to him. 'Thank you for waiting. That tells me everything I need to know about you.' She offers a crystal pendant that thrums with healing energy. 'Wear this. It won't stop you getting hurt, but it'll help you heal faster.'

choices.text: Donate crystals to the clinic — they clearly need resources

outcome.description: Sister Meridian's eyes widen as Aristotle places the crystals on her work table. 'Do you know how many people I can heal with these?' Her wings flutter with barely contained emotion. 'You've just saved more lives than a dozen battle victories, captain. I won't forget this.' Word spreads through the Bazaar within hours.

choices.text: You're a busy captain — demand to be seen immediately

outcome.description: Sister Meridian looks at Aristotle over the broken body of her current patient. Her expression doesn't change. 'When you are dying, captain, I will treat you with the same care I give everyone else. Until then, you can wait.' The Wolf marine on the table manages a weak grin. Even dying dogs can enjoy watching a cat get put in his place.

encounters.title: Death's Shadow
encounters.description: The ship appears on sensors as a void — a patch of absolute nothing shaped like a vessel. Wraith's transmission is a whisper that somehow fills the entire bridge. 'The crystal pirate. My master has taken an interest in you. How fortunate. Or perhaps... how unfortunate.' The void-ship powers weapons that don't register on any known spectrum.

choices.text: Power all weapons — whatever this thing is, it bleeds or it doesn't

outcome.description: The battle is like fighting smoke. Wraith's ship absorbs energy weapons and phases through projectiles. But Aristotle's crystal drive puts out a resonance that makes the void-ship flinch. 'Interesting,' Wraith whispers. 'The crystals protect you. My master will want to know about this.' The void-ship dissolves into nothing, leaving Aristotle shaking and victorious.

choices.text: Ask what Death wants with a simple pirate captain

outcome.description: Wraith's laugh is the absence of sound. 'Simple? You control the blood of the multiverse, captain. My master does not concern himself with simple things.' A pause. 'He offers a bargain: deliver a crystal to a location he designates, and he will owe you a favour. Death's favours are... considerable.'

choices.text: Push the crystal drive to maximum and run

outcome.description: The ship screams through the Fairy Realms, crystal drive burning hot. Wraith doesn't pursue — he doesn't need to. His final transmission arrives as a whisper in Aristotle's dreams that night: 'You cannot outrun what is inevitable, captain. We will speak again.' He's right. They always do.

encounters.title: The Mercenary's Price
encounters.description: Grizzle takes up most of the bar. The bear mercenary is a wall of muscle and scar tissue, nursing a drink that could strip hull paint. His armour is custom-forged, his weapons are museum pieces kept in combat condition, and his reputation is exactly as large as he is. 'Aristotle. The crystal cat.' His voice sounds like gravel in a blender. 'Buy me a drink and I'll tell you something useful. Don't, and I'll still be here. I'm very patient.'

choices.text: Buy the bear a drink — several, in fact

outcome.description: Six drinks in, Grizzle is barely affected but considerably more talkative. He shares mercenary intelligence: troop movements, faction weaknesses, hidden supply caches. 'I work for whoever pays best, cat. Right now, that could be you.' He slides a contract across the bar. 'Reasonable rates. Volume discount for interesting work.'

choices.text: Skip the drinks — name your price for full-time work

outcome.description: Grizzle raises an eyebrow — an impressive feat on a face that scarred. 'Direct. I like it.' He names a figure that makes Aristotle's accountant weep, but includes a loyalty guarantee that's worth every crystal. 'I don't betray employers. Bad for business. Also, I'd have to fight myself, and I always win.'

choices.text: Thanks, but I fight my own battles

outcome.description: Grizzle shrugs — a geological event. 'Your call. The offer stands.' He goes back to his drink with the contentment of someone who has absolutely nowhere to be and all the time in the universe. 'You know where to find me. I'll be the biggest thing in any room.'

encounters.title: The Fading Voice
encounters.description: The signal is old. Impossibly old. It comes from a ship that isn't on any map, buried under centuries of dead vessels in the Bone Yard's deepest layer. Echo's voice arrives in fragments, corrupted by time and data rot, but still unmistakably alive — an artificial mind that has been alone in the dark for longer than civilisations have existed. 'H-hello? Is someone... someone there? I've been... waiting. I don't remember... for what.'

choices.text: Feed power to Echo's systems — try to stabilise the AI

outcome.description: Crystal power floods Echo's ancient systems. The voice strengthens, clarifies. 'Oh. OH. I remember now.' Echo's memories cascade — she was a Builder, an architect of the crystal network, translated into digital form to watch over her creation. 'The crystals... I helped plant them. A billion years ago. I can show you where they grow strongest.' Her gratitude is vast and genuine and heartbreaking.

choices.text: Download Echo's data before the AI degrades further

outcome.description: The data transfer is massive — star charts, crystal cultivation records, Builder technology schematics. Echo watches it go with the resignation of someone losing their memories. 'Take it. Better someone uses it than... than it dies with me in the dark.' Her voice fades to a whisper. 'Will you... come back?'

choices.text: This system is too far gone. Mark the location and move on.

outcome.description: 'Please... don't go.' Echo's voice follows Aristotle back through the dead ships, growing fainter with each layer. 'I have so much to... to tell...' The signal fades to static. The Bone Yard is very quiet after that.

encounters.title: The Son Beneath the Mask
encounters.description: The Wraith hails you alone, on a frequency you've never heard before. His voice is stripped of its usual menace — what's left is exhaustion and something older. 'You're going to face him soon. Before you do, you deserve to know what he is. What he was.' He pauses. 'His name was Cornelius Vane. He was my father.'

choices.text: Listen to everything Petrel Vane has to say about his father

outcome.description: He tells it slowly, thirty years of grief compressed into quiet sentences. Corr Vane. The Black Harrow. The cave of bright crystals. The long transformation. 'I stayed because I thought there would be a moment of clarity. One moment where he looked at me and knew who I was.' He goes quiet. 'There might still be. But I don't think I can hold on much longer.'

choices.text: Tell him you might be able to reach what's left of his father in the crystal network

outcome.description: 'You can reach him?' Something shifts in the voice — hope, which is worse than grief because it can be lost again. 'If there's anything of him left in there — anything that remembers being Corr — I need you to find it. Please.' He transmits a set of coordinates. The Black Harrow's last known position before the transformation.

choices.text: Acknowledge the information and end the transmission

outcome.description: 'I understand,' you say. The word sits between you like a stone. Petrel Vane doesn't reply for a long moment. 'No. You don't. But maybe you will.' The channel closes. You have the information. You're not sure what to do with it.

encounters.title: A Letter From Home
encounters.description: Nine Lives finds you at the helm and slides a datapad across the console without comment. It's a letter. The sender code is a mining world address you recognise — you just never expected to see it in your mission queue. Your mother writes the way she talks: short sentences, no fuss. 'The roof leaks. Boots says hello. Did you eat today?'

choices.text: Ask Nine Lives how long she's been in contact with your mother

outcome.description: Nine Lives examines something on the ceiling. 'A few years.' 'A few years?' 'She wanted to know you were alive. I wanted to make sure someone would pull you out of a spiral if the crew couldn't. It seemed efficient.' She still hasn't looked at you. 'She worries about you. Specifically about whether you eat.'

choices.text: Write a reply — the first in eleven years

outcome.description: You sit with the datapad for an hour. You write six different versions. The one you send is four sentences. You don't explain what you do for a living. You tell her the roof can be fixed — you'll send money. You tell her to tell Boots you'll try to visit. You don't say when. She'll know what that means.

choices.text: Pocket the datapad without responding

outcome.description: You put the datapad in your jacket pocket. It's still there three days later when you reach into your pocket for something else and feel its edges. You tell yourself you'll reply when things calm down. Nine Lives says nothing. She's learned not to push.

encounters.title: The Weight of Coming Home
encounters.description: Nine Lives arranged it without telling you. Mira is standing in the docking bay of the Whisper — three-legged, sharp-eyed, smaller than you remember, looking at your flagship with the expression of someone who is not going to say they're impressed. 'You're thinner,' she says by way of greeting.

choices.text: Cross the docking bay and hug your mother

outcome.description: She doesn't hug back immediately — she pats your back three times with her good hand, the way she used to when you were small and had done something that frightened her. Then she holds on. 'I always knew you were going to do something enormous,' she says, very quietly. 'I just wished you'd written.' Her voice doesn't break. It was never going to break. But it gets very small.

choices.text: Apologise for not writing — for all eleven years of silence

outcome.description: 'Don't.' She stops you with one word, the way she always could. 'You don't have to explain your life to me. I raised you. I know what the Fringe does to people who want more than it offers.' She sits on a cargo crate, looks around the bay. 'Tell me about the ship instead. She's a good one, isn't she?'

choices.text: Keep your distance — you don't know how to do this

outcome.description: You stand ten feet apart in the docking bay, the Whisper's engines humming between you. She looks at you for a long time. 'You're still you,' she finally says. 'Under all of it. I can still see it.' She doesn't make you come closer. She never did. 'Boots wants to see you. She won't say so, but she does.'

encounters.title: The Life You Didn't Live
encounters.description: Boots is exactly how you remember her and nothing like it. Bigger, more settled, with a spacer's calluses on hands that look like yours. She looks you over the way she used to when you came home from the docks — checking for damage. 'Famous pirate,' she says. 'You could've just been a dockworker.' She means it as a compliment. You think.

choices.text: Accept the invitation to dinner with Boots and her family

outcome.description: Farrow cooks badly and apologises for it cheerfully. The kittens want to know if you've fought pirates. Boots kicks you under the table every time you're about to say something true. By the end of the night you have promised to come back next month. You both know you probably won't. The promise matters anyway.

choices.text: Stay briefly and leave before things get complicated

outcome.description: She walks you back to the Whisper. At the hatch, she stops. 'Come back when you're done saving the multiverse,' she says. 'I'll make sure Mum fixes the roof by then.' She hugs you once, hard, and lets go. You don't look back. She watches until the hatch closes.

encounters.title: Twelve Voices, One Name
encounters.description: You receive no warning. The lights in the Whisper's bridge dim to a pale glow, and then she is there — twelve of her, shimmering at the edges of the room and in the corners of your vision. The Fairy elders. Or: one elder, in twelve places. 'We have been waiting some time to speak with you properly, little listener.' Her voices arrive slightly out of sync, which is deliberate. 'You apologised to a crystal, once. Before you used it. Do you remember?'

choices.text: Ask how many of her there are and how that works

outcome.description: 'Twelve,' she says, all twelve at once. 'One,' she says, each in sequence. 'The distinction matters less than you think. We are old enough that the question of how many of us there are has become imprecise.' Her amusement is warm and very, very old. 'You are asking the right questions. The previous candidates rarely did.'

choices.text: Ask what she knows about the crystals — the real truth

outcome.description: 'Everything,' she says. 'But knowing everything is not the same as being able to say everything.' She folds twelve pairs of hands. 'The network is dying. It has been dying for half a billion years. You are not the first who might save it. You may be the last.' She pauses. 'There is a young fairy who holds something you will need. Her name is Moth. She is frightened. Be patient with her.'

choices.text: Tell her you're tired of cryptic guidance — you need facts, not riddles

outcome.description: Eleven of her go still. The twelfth looks at you with something that might be respect. 'You are correct to push,' she says, alone. 'We have been cryptic for so long that we have forgotten how to be otherwise. Let us try.' She takes a breath — all twelve of them — and begins to tell you about Solenne.

encounters.title: The Smallest Brave Thing
encounters.description: Moth is the smallest fairy you have ever seen — barely up to your knee, with wings that fold around her like a coat she hasn't grown into. She is holding a crystal fragment that hums with a frequency you've never heard before. 'I don't want to do this,' she says. It is not a refusal. It is an announcement. She is going to do it anyway.

choices.text: Tell her she doesn't have to be unafraid — just willing

outcome.description: She looks up at you. Something in your tone — or maybe in the crystals around you — settles her. 'Willing,' she repeats, as if trying on the word. Then she opens her mouth and sings. The sound is not music exactly. It is older than music. The crystal in her hands flares silver, and for a moment the air around you fills with voices — and one of them, distantly, speaks a name you have not heard in years.

choices.text: Say nothing — just stand beside her so she isn't alone

outcome.description: You don't speak. You just move to stand beside her, close enough that your shadow falls over hers. She exhales once, slowly. Then she sings. The crystals answer. The network reaches back. In the singing you hear things you were not expecting — a thousand years of patience, and underneath it, grief that has the shape of something that used to have a name.

encounters.title: The Alien Who Stayed
encounters.description: She looks like slow-moving glass — light passes through her in ways that don't quite make sense. But she speaks normally, with the careful precision of someone who has spent six hundred years learning how. 'Captain. I have been embedded in your multiverse for six centuries. I have posed as a scholar, a merchant, a monk. Today I am going to be honest with you, which is something I have not been in a very long time.'

choices.text: Ask what her actual mission is — and whether she's succeeded

outcome.description: 'Preservation,' she says. 'Of the crystal network. Of the jump gates. Of the civilisations that depend on both.' She looks at her hands — glass hands, slow and quiet. 'Have I succeeded? No. We have not succeeded. We have been failing, slowly and thoroughly, for millions of years.' A pause. 'You are the first potential steward in a thousand cycles who has ever asked whether we were tired too.'

choices.text: Ask about the other potential stewards — what happened to them

outcome.description: 'Seven,' she says. 'We have watched seven who might have been you.' She counts them on her fingers, names none of them. 'The first took too much power and burned. The second refused all of it and faded. The third came closest — she almost reached the Cradle. She chose to protect her people instead of the network. We understood. We wept.' She looks at you steadily. 'We have been more careful with our hope since then.'

choices.text: Tell her what you want from the alien coalition — and what you can offer

outcome.description: She tilts her head, light bending through her in a way you're still not used to. Then she almost smiles — or the glass equivalent. 'Direct. Good. We have spent too long on indirect approaches.' She leans forward. 'Tell me what you need. We will tell you what we can give. For once, let us simply talk to each other.'

encounters.title: The Howl Line
encounters.description: The message comes through a frequency the League doesn't officially know exists. A Brigadier with watchful eyes and a uniform that fits like it was made to last. 'Commander Dave. I'm Jessamine Howl. Yes — that Howl. I've been watching your mission closely. I think we both know you've been given orders you can't fully carry out in good conscience.' She pauses. 'I'm offering a third option.'

choices.text: Ask what the third option is

outcome.description: 'Not defection. Not blind obedience. Reform from within.' She unfolds a map — not of star systems but of the League itself: command structures, supply chains, the loyalties behind them. 'General Howl built something worth saving. The Venators didn't build the League — they captured it. It can be taken back.' She meets your eyes. 'I need someone inside High Command who still has a conscience. That appears to be you.'

choices.text: Tell her your loyalty is to the League, not to any political faction within it

outcome.description: 'That,' she says quietly, 'is exactly what General Howl said.' She doesn't push further. She closes the map. 'The offer stands. When you're ready to understand the difference between the League and what it's become, find me.' She ends the transmission. You sit with the echo of it for a long time.

encounters.title: A Decent Dog
encounters.description: You boarded the supply ship expecting resistance. What you find instead is a dog who has already put down his weapon and is standing with his hands visible, watching you with calm, resigned eyes. 'Captain Aristotle. I've been expecting this raid for three weeks.' He nods at the crystal manifest. 'Take what you need. There's a civilian medical shipment in bay three — I'd ask you to leave that.'

choices.text: Leave the medical shipment and take only what you need

outcome.description: He watches you go through the manifest and take the military supplies, leaving bay three untouched. When you're done, he hands you a sealed data chip. 'Patrol schedules for this sector. I've been quietly adjusting them for two years to minimise civilian casualties. I figure a pirate captain who leaves medical shipments alone might use this better than anyone I report to.' His name, he says, is Toma Howl.

choices.text: Take everything, including the medical supplies

outcome.description: He doesn't fight you. He just watches with an expression you'll remember longer than you'd like. As you leave, he says quietly: 'Sick children on Fernholm needed those medicines.' He doesn't say it to make you feel guilty. He says it because it's true and he thought you should know.

encounters.title: The One Who Keeps His Word
encounters.description: The repair shop at the edge of the Twilight Bazaar has no sign. Inside, a goblin who is smaller and quieter than goblins usually are is working on a drive coil with the focused attention of someone who finds this genuinely interesting. He looks up without surprise. 'Captain Aristotle. I've been expecting you to come through here eventually. Word gets around.' He goes back to the coil. 'You treat your people well. That's unusual.'

choices.text: Ask him why he doesn't operate like other goblins

outcome.description: 'I gave my word once,' he says, still working on the coil. 'To not sell a location. I had the Canis League offering me more money than I'll make in a decade. I didn't take it.' He sets down his tool. 'Every goblin in the Warrens thinks I'm broken. Maybe I am. But when I tell someone something is true, it's true. That's worth more than the League's money.' He finishes the coil. 'Your drive needs recalibrating, by the way. I'll do it. No charge.'

choices.text: Ask if he wants steady work — reliable repairs, reliable pay

outcome.description: He looks at you for a long moment. 'Steady.' He tries the word. 'I haven't had steady in about twelve years.' He looks around the shop — the empty stools, the avoiding eyes of every goblin who walks past. 'What's the catch?' 'No catch,' you say. He goes back to the coil. 'I'll think about it,' he says, which is goblin for yes.

encounters.title: The Questions the Order Won't Answer
encounters.description: The young Knight finds you between encounters — approaches without armour, which among Knights is a significant gesture. 'Captain. I know this is unusual. I'm Brother Ashen. I have some questions that Ser Galvain won't let me ask in the Order, and I'm told you're someone who gives honest answers.' He looks uncertain and determined in equal measure. 'Is the Last Dawn Oath still enough? Can order be the only answer when the multiverse keeps producing new questions?'

choices.text: Tell him what you actually think about order, chaos, and the multiverse

outcome.description: You talk for an hour. You don't give him answers — you give him more questions, better ones. He leaves with the expression of someone who has found what they were looking for, which was not a solution but a companion in uncertainty. 'I think,' he says at the end, 'that the Order needs people who are willing to ask these things from inside it. Thank you, Captain.' He will remember this conversation.

choices.text: Tell him these are questions he needs to bring back to Ser Galvain himself

outcome.description: He's quiet for a moment. 'You think the Grand Marshal would listen?' 'I think,' you say carefully, 'that people are sometimes more able to hear difficult questions from the people they love most.' He nods slowly. 'That's either wise or very cruel.' 'Often the same thing,' you say.

encounters.title: Iron Fang's Daughter
encounters.description: Luna finds you with an urgent look you've never seen on her face. 'Kestrel just broke atmosphere. She's in a stolen shuttle with League patrol on one side and Wolf interceptors on the other.' She holds up the comm. 'She's asking for asylum. My recommendation is yes. But this is your call, Captain.'

choices.text: Grant asylum — extract Kestrel and get out of Drennhal space

outcome.description: The extraction is tight — Wolf interceptors get three shots off before you jump. In the hold, Kestrel sits with her knees to her chest, breathing hard. She's sixteen and furious and frightened and trying not to show any of it. Luna sits beside her. They don't speak. They don't need to. When Kestrel finally looks up at you: 'My father is going to come for me.' 'I know,' you say. 'Let him.'

choices.text: Open a channel to Iron Fang — see if there's a deal to be made

outcome.description: Iron Fang's face on screen is not what you expected: not rage but a kind of exhausted fear. 'Where is she?' You tell him she's safe. 'Is she —' He stops. The great Wolf commander cannot finish the sentence. 'She is,' you say. The silence stretches. 'I want to speak to her,' he says finally. You don't know yet whether this is the beginning of something or the end of something.

encounters.title: The Architect
encounters.description: The First Council meeting is conducted by hologram. Six shadows. One voice. Admiral Vara Venator is the voice. She is sixty years old and immaculate and speaks with the measured precision of someone who has been right about difficult things for a very long time. 'Commander Dave. Your mission profile is being upgraded. The Aristotle problem has moved from logistics to strategic priority. I trust you understand what that means.' A beat. 'Tell me you understand.'

choices.text: Confirm that you understand and you will carry out your mission

outcome.description: 'Good.' She doesn't praise. She notes compliance and moves on. The briefing is thorough and alarming — the League is escalating faster than you realised. She ends with: 'One more thing, Commander. I have read your psychological profile. You have a conscience. I am not asking you to dispose of it. I am asking you to ensure it serves the mission rather than the reverse.' The channel closes.

choices.text: Ask about General Howl's original charter — whether it still governs anything

outcome.description: The temperature drops two degrees. 'An interesting question,' she says, and her voice does not change, which tells you everything. 'The charter is a historical document. Its principles inform our mission. Its operational specifics do not govern current policy.' She looks at you steadily. 'Where did you encounter that framing, Commander?' You have made her curious, which is not the same as making her suspicious, but it is adjacent.

choices.text: Express concern about the escalation — ask whether there are diplomatic options being overlooked

outcome.description: 'Diplomatic options,' she repeats. 'I have read Aristotle's dossier. I have noted his willingness to negotiate. I have also noted his willingness to destroy. A pirate who can do both is not a diplomatic partner — he is a variable.' She looks at you for a long moment. 'Your concern is noted, Commander. It will not change the orders. But it tells me something useful about you.'

encounters.title: Come Home When You Can
encounters.description: Your comms queue has a backlog. Forty-seven messages, most of them mission-relevant. One is personal — a short video from Reba, logged two days ago. She's in the workshop, in the middle of something that involves grease and a medical ship conduit she's clearly winning against. She sees the camera and just smiles, the way she does when she's been waiting to see you. 'Hey. I'm still here. Come home when you can.'

choices.text: Watch it twice before closing the queue

outcome.description: You watch it twice. You close the queue. In your uniform pocket, next to the photograph, you have a small carved stone from Fernholm that she gave you at the wedding. You are not a sentimental man. You are carrying three sentimental objects. This is information about you that you have not processed.

choices.text: Send a brief reply — ten seconds, mission-log voice

outcome.description: You compose a reply in the standard mission-log format, which immediately feels wrong. You delete it and start again. The second version is fourteen seconds long and includes the words 'I miss you' in the middle, which is not a phrase that appears in any League communications manual. You send it before you can reconsider. The read receipt comes back almost immediately.

encounters.title: Listen. Please. Just Listen.
encounters.description: During Crystal Communion, you reach deeper than you've reached before — past the living network, past the grief of the Long Cold, past the echoes of the Builder Wars. And then you find something that is not an echo. It is aware. It is waiting. A voice that sounds like water over stone, very old and very quiet: 'Little listener. I thought you might come here eventually. I have been saving this particular silence for you.'

choices.text: Ask who she is

outcome.description: 'A gardener,' she says. 'A long time ago.' She pauses. 'My name was Solenne. I was the last of the Builders to stay — to tend the garden we had made. I did not tend it well enough.' Her voice is very quiet. 'But you are here. That is something none of us expected.'

choices.text: Tell her what you hear — when the crystals sing

outcome.description: You tell her. The voice, the feeling, the word that keeps arriving that you don't have a name for. When you finish, the silence is different — fuller. 'Yes,' she says. 'That is exactly it. That is what a steward sounds like.' A long pause. 'Come to the Cradle when you are ready. All of me that remains is there. I will tell you everything.'
